experiences.name: Mercado de San Juan Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Mexico City's most beloved gourmet markets, sampling exotic cheeses, fresh seafood tostadas, traditional tacos, and artisanal products. Chat with local vendors and taste authentic Mexican flavors in a vibrant market setting.

experiences.name: Museo Nacional de Antropología Visit
experiences.description: Discover one of the world's greatest anthropology museums, housing the famous Aztec Sun Stone and vast collections of pre-Columbian artifacts. Gain deep insight into Mexico's rich indigenous civilizations and cultural heritage across 23 exhibition halls.

experiences.name: Coyoacán Neighborhood Walking Tour & Street Food
experiences.description: Wander through the cobblestone streets of Frida Kahlo's historic neighborhood, visiting the colorful Mercado de Coyoacán for traditional tlayudas, tostadas, and fresh aguas frescas. Explore the bohemian plazas and vibrant local street art scene.

experiences.name: Tacos al Pastor Crawl in La Roma
experiences.description: Embark on a self-guided taco crawl through the trendy Roma neighborhood, stopping at legendary taquerías like El Huequito and local street stands. Sample Mexico City's iconic al pastor, suadero, and carnitas tacos paired with handmade salsas.

experiences.name: Teotihuacán Pyramids Day Trip
experiences.description: Journey to the ancient pre-Aztec city of Teotihuacán and climb the iconic Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon. Explore the Avenue of the Dead, admire ancient murals, and learn about one of Mesoamerica's most powerful civilizations with a local guide.
experiences.location: Teotihuacán, State of Mexico (50 km northeast of Mexico City)

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 13:00. Use morning for in-flight rest and preparation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Aeropuerto Internacional Benito Juárez at 13:00. Take the Metro Line 5 (Terminal Aérea station) to the city center – one of the cheapest airport transfers available (approx. 5 MXN). Check in to your boutique stay in Centro Histórico. Once settled, take a relaxed self-guided walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), Mexico City's massive main square. Admire the Metropolitan Cathedral (free entry) and the National Palace exterior. Soak in the energy of street performers and vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Calle Regina, a lively pedestrian street in Centro Histórico filled with local life, street food stalls, and affordable cantinas. Browse the evening atmosphere and pick up a snack from a street vendor.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap comida corrida (set lunch menu) near the Zócalo at a local fonda or market stall – expect to pay 60–90 MXN for soup, main course, and a drink.
meals.dinner: Tacos at a street taqueria on or near Calle Regina. Try tacos de canasta or tacos al pastor – 15–25 MXN per taco. Budget total: ~80 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Metro is the cheapest and fastest way from the airport. Avoid taxis hailed on the street; use authorized airport taxis or the Metro. Keep your belongings secure in crowded areas. Exchange some cash before leaving the airport or use an ATM inside the terminal.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day early with a visit to the Templo Mayor archaeological site (entry ~80 MXN with student discount, or free on Sundays – note this is Tuesday). Explore the ruins of the ancient Aztec temple right in the heart of Centro Histórico and visit the on-site museum included in the ticket price. Afterward, walk to the nearby Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire its stunning Art Nouveau exterior and peek inside the lobby for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Mercado de San Juan (about 15 minutes walk from Centro), a vibrant local market beloved by both residents and chefs. Browse exotic ingredients, cheeses, and international foods. Then walk to Alameda Central, the city's oldest public park, for a relaxing stroll. Visit the Museo Mural Diego Rivera (entry ~45 MXN) to see the famous 'Sueño de una Tarde Dominical' mural.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Barrio de Tepito market area from a safe distance or head to Plaza Garibaldi (a 15-minute walk from Centro) to experience mariachi music live in the plaza – listening is free, though buying a drink at a pulquería nearby is a fun local experience.

meals.breakfast: Tamales and atole from a street vendor near the hotel – a classic Mexico City breakfast for around 30–40 MXN.
meals.lunch: Comida corrida at a local restaurant inside or near Mercado de San Juan – 70–100 MXN for a full set meal with agua fresca.
meals.dinner: Pozole or sopa azteca at a budget-friendly restaurant near Alameda Central – around 80–120 MXN per bowl. Look for places with handwritten menus on chalkboards, a sign of authenticity and value.

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays – Tuesday is perfect. Wear comfortable walking shoes as you'll cover 4–6 km on foot. Carry a reusable water bottle; purified water refill stations are available in markets.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro (Line 2, Tasqueña direction, change at Hidalgo to Line 3 toward Universidad) to Coyoacán – about 45 minutes and only 5 MXN. Visit the Museo Casa Frida Kahlo (the Blue House) – book tickets online in advance as they sell out (entry ~270 MXN, worth every peso). Explore Frida Kahlo's iconic home, her art, and personal belongings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Mercado de Coyoacán for lunch and browse artisan crafts and souvenirs. Then explore the charming cobblestone streets and plazas of Coyoacán, including Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo. Visit the free Museo Nacional de Culturas Populares to learn about Mexican folk art and traditions.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico via Metro. Spend the evening exploring the lit-up historic streets. Visit a local pulquería (traditional fermented agave drink bar) for an authentic and very affordable evening drink – pulque is a true local experience and costs around 30–50 MXN per glass.

meals.breakfast: Chilaquiles or enfrijoladas at a small café or fonda near your hotel – 60–90 MXN, a hearty and traditional Mexican breakfast.
meals.lunch: Tostadas de tinga or tlayudas from a market stall inside Mercado de Coyoacán – 40–70 MXN. Fresh, delicious, and deeply local.
meals.dinner: Street tacos back in Centro Histórico – try a different style tonight such as tacos de suadero or carnitas. Budget ~80–100 MXN for a satisfying dinner with a agua de jamaica.

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets at least 2–3 days in advance via their official website to avoid sellouts. Coyoacán is very walkable and safe for tourists. The Metro journey is an experience in itself – a great way to observe everyday city life.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Chapultepec (Line 1, Observatorio direction). Enter Bosque de Chapultepec, one of the largest urban parks in the world – entry is free. Visit the Castillo de Chapultepec (entry ~85 MXN), a hilltop castle with panoramic views of the city and home to the National History Museum. Explore the exhibits covering Mexican history from pre-Hispanic times to the modern era.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the park to the Museo Nacional de Antropología – one of the world's greatest museums (entry ~85 MXN, free on Sundays). Spend 2–3 hours exploring extraordinary pre-Columbian artifacts including the famous Aztec Sun Stone. Afterward, stroll through the upscale Polanco neighborhood nearby to window-shop and people-watch without spending a peso.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Centro or explore Colonia Roma (Metro Line 1 to Insurgentes). Walk along Álvaro Obregón avenue, lined with trees, sculptures, and local cafés. Browse a tianguis (street market) if one is active in the area.

meals.breakfast: Molletes (toasted bolillo rolls with beans and cheese) at a neighborhood café near your hotel – around 50–70 MXN with coffee.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic from a nearby market or grab tortas (Mexican sandwiches) from a street vendor near Chapultepec Park – 40–60 MXN each, eat on a park bench surrounded by nature.
meals.dinner: Explore Colonia Roma's budget-friendly taco spots or try a bowl of caldo de pollo (chicken broth soup) at a local fondita – 70–100 MXN. Roma has excellent value street food despite being a trendy neighborhood.

day_by_day.notes: Chapultepec Park is massive – wear comfortable shoes and pace yourself. The Anthropology Museum alone could take a full day; prioritize the Mexica (Aztec) and Maya halls if time is limited. Sunday is free entry day for both museums if you want to revisit.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your final morning revisiting your favorite spots in Centro Histórico. Visit the interior of the Metropolitan Cathedral (free) and explore the ornate baroque chapels inside. Walk to the Secretaría de Educación Pública (SEP building) to see Diego Rivera's incredible murals covering the interior courtyard walls – entry is free with ID. A hidden gem that most tourists miss.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mercado de Artesanías La Ciudadela, the best place in the city to buy authentic Mexican crafts and souvenirs at fair prices (about 10 minutes walk from Centro). Browse handmade textiles, ceramics, silver jewelry, and folk art. Practice your bargaining skills respectfully. Afterward, visit the nearby Biblioteca de México inside the Ciudadela complex – a beautiful free cultural space.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your last night with a special but still budget-friendly dinner. Head to a local cantina in Centro for a traditional Mexican meal. Many cantinas offer free botanas (small snacks/appetizers) with drink orders – a wonderful old Mexico City tradition. Enjoy the festive Friday atmosphere of the city.

meals.breakfast: Huevos rancheros or huevos a la mexicana at a neighborhood fonda – 60–80 MXN, a classic and filling farewell breakfast.
meals.lunch: Gorditas or quesadillas from a market stall near La Ciudadela – 20–35 MXN each. Try huitlacoche (corn fungus) or flor de calabaza (squash blossom) fillings for a uniquely Mexican experience.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last night at a well-regarded local cantina such as one of the historic cantinas in Centro Histórico. A full meal with a mezcal or craft beer should still come in under 250–300 MXN – excellent value for a memorable final evening.

day_by_day.notes: La Ciudadela market is great for last-minute shopping – prices are fair but still negotiable. Keep some cash in MXN for final purchases. The SEP murals by Rivera are genuinely world-class and completely free – don't skip them. Consider a late-night walk around the illuminated Zócalo as a final farewell to this incredible city.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Check in to your boutique hotel in Centro Histórico, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest public squares in the world. Visit the exterior of the Palacio Nacional and the Catedral Metropolitana. Stroll along Calle Madero, a pedestrian street lined with colonial architecture, shops, and street performers.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively streets of Centro Histórico as they light up at night. Visit the rooftop bar at Gran Hotel Ciudad de México for a stunning view of the Zócalo illuminated. Wind down with a relaxed dinner nearby.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick and authentic bite at Mercado de San Juan (a short taxi ride) or a torta from a local street stall near the Zócalo — budget around 80–150 MXN
meals.dinner: Dinner at Café de Tacuba, a historic Mexico City institution serving traditional Mexican cuisine since 1912. Try the enchiladas or mole dishes. Mid-range pricing around 200–350 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first afternoon light to recover from travel. Exchange some currency at a reputable casa de cambio near the hotel rather than at the airport for better rates. Wear comfortable walking shoes — Centro Histórico is best explored on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Palacio Nacional to see Diego Rivera's iconic murals depicting the history of Mexico — entry is free. Arrive early (doors open at 9:00) to beat the crowds. Afterward, explore the adjacent Templo Mayor archaeological site and its museum, the ruins of the main Aztec temple of Tenochtitlán.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Mercado de San Juan for a deep dive into local food culture — sample artisan cheeses, exotic fruits, fresh juices, and international ingredients. Then walk to the nearby Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture and check out any current exhibitions inside.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Alameda Central park as the sun sets, then head to the Barrio Chino (Chinatown) area or nearby streets for a casual evening. End the night with mezcal tasting at a local mezcalería in Centro Histórico.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at El Cardinal, a classic Mexico City breakfast spot near the Zócalo. Try the chilaquiles or tamales with café de olla. Budget around 150–250 MXN.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mercado de San Juan — build your own meal from market stalls. Try a tostada de mariscos or a fresh torta. Budget around 100–180 MXN.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Los Girasoles, a well-regarded restaurant near Palacio de Bellas Artes offering pre-Hispanic and traditional Mexican cuisine in a relaxed setting. Budget around 250–400 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor entry costs around 85 MXN (subject to change). The Palacio de Bellas Artes has free entry to the ground floor; upper galleries may have a small fee. Carry a light jacket as March mornings can be cool at 2,240m altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Take a metro or Uber to Coyoacán neighborhood (about 30–40 minutes from Centro). Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (Casa Azul), the famous Blue House where Frida Kahlo was born and lived. Book tickets online in advance as they sell out quickly. Afterward, explore the cobblestone streets and colonial architecture of the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Mercado de Coyoacán for lunch and browse artisan crafts, fresh produce, and street food. Then visit the nearby Museo León Trotsky, the home where the Russian revolutionary lived in exile and was assassinated. Return to Centro Histórico in the late afternoon via Uber or metro.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening in Centro Histórico. Visit the rooftop terrace of a nearby bar for sunset views over the city skyline, then explore the illuminated streets around Plaza Garibaldi to hear mariachi bands perform live.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a local café in Centro before heading out. Alternatively, grab fresh fruit, a tamale, or a quesadilla from a street vendor near the metro — budget 50–100 MXN.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mercado de Coyoacán — try the famous tostadas de tinga or enfrijoladas from the market stalls. Budget around 80–150 MXN.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Contramar (book ahead) in nearby Colonia Roma — a beloved Mexico City seafood restaurant. Try the tuna tostadas and grilled fish. Budget around 300–500 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Museo Frida Kahlo tickets at least a week in advance at museofridakahlo.org.mx — they sell out fast. Coyoacán is very walkable and safe for tourists. Plaza Garibaldi is lively but watch your belongings in crowds at night.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early Uber or organized tour to Teotihuacán, the ancient pre-Columbian city located about 50 km northeast of Mexico City (approximately 1 hour by car). Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon, and walk the Avenue of the Dead. Arrive by 9:00 to avoid midday heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City by early afternoon. Head to Colonia Roma or Colonia Condesa, two of the city's hippest neighborhoods, for a relaxed afternoon. Explore the Art Deco architecture, browse independent bookshops, and people-watch in Parque México or Parque España.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening in Colonia Roma or Condesa, which have a fantastic dining and bar scene. Browse the street art in the area and enjoy a casual evening dinner before heading back to Centro Histórico.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — grab a coffee and a pan dulce (sweet bread) from a local panadería near your hotel. Budget 40–80 MXN.
meals.lunch: Lunch near Teotihuacán at La Gruta, a restaurant dramatically set inside a natural cave near the archaeological site. Try the traditional Mexican set menu. Budget around 250–400 MXN per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Expendio de Maíz Sin Nombre in Colonia Roma — a rustic, creative Mexican restaurant celebrating native corn and traditional techniques. Budget around 300–450 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Teotihuacán entry costs around 85 MXN. Wear sunscreen, a hat, and bring water — the site is vast and exposed. The site opens at 9:00 and closes at 17:00. Consider hiring a local guide at the entrance for deeper historical context (negotiate around 300–500 MXN for a 2-hour tour).

day_by_day.morning: Spend your last morning revisiting any highlights in Centro Histórico you may have missed. Visit the Museo del Templo Mayor if you skipped it earlier, or duck into the Biblioteca Miguel Lerdo de Tejada, a stunning baroque library. Browse the antique and book market at Plaza del Ángel or nearby street stalls for souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museo Nacional de Arte (MUNAL) near the Zócalo, which houses an impressive collection of Mexican art from the 16th to 20th centuries. Afterward, take a final walk through the streets of Centro, pick up last-minute souvenirs like artisan crafts, talavera pottery, or local spices at nearby markets.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Centro Histórico with views of the illuminated Zócalo. Reflect on the trip over a final round of traditional Mexican cocktails — a mezcal negroni or a classic margarita with sal de gusano.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at a classic local spot — try Hostería de Santo Domingo, one of Mexico City's oldest restaurants, for traditional chiles en nogada (seasonal) or egg dishes. Budget around 150–250 MXN.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a street taco stand in Centro — order tacos de canasta or tacos al pastor from a popular local spot. Budget around 60–120 MXN.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Azul Histórico, a beautiful restaurant set in a courtyard garden in Centro Histórico, serving elevated traditional Mexican cuisine. Budget around 350–550 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: MUNAL entry is around 85 MXN and free on Sundays. If departing on Day 6, pack your bags the night before and confirm your airport transfer. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for Mexico City's Benito Juárez International Airport, especially during peak hours.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Mexico City International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer arranged from airport to boutique hotel in Centro Histórico via luxury sedan service.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in and freshen up at the boutique hotel, then take a leisurely guided walking tour of the immediate surroundings: admire the iconic Palacio de Bellas Artes façade, stroll along the pedestrian Madero Street, and explore the historic Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Visit the Catedral Metropolitana for a glimpse of its stunning baroque interior.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks on a rooftop bar overlooking the Zócalo — Bar La Opera or the rooftop of Gran Hotel Ciudad de México is ideal for first-night ambiance. Follow with a welcome dinner showcasing refined Mexican cuisine.

meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at Azul Histórico, a celebrated restaurant set in a beautiful courtyard in Centro Histórico, known for elevated regional Mexican dishes and fresh agua frescas.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Contramar (reserve in advance) or El Cardenal Centro Histórico — a Mexico City institution serving traditional Mexican breakfast and dinner classics with premium ingredients in an elegant colonial setting.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm hotel early check-in if possible given the 13:00 arrival. Stay hydrated — Mexico City sits at 2,240m altitude and mild altitude adjustment is common on day one.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the day with a deep cultural immersion at the Templo Mayor Archaeological Site and its world-class museum, located just steps from the Zócalo. This Aztec ceremonial center offers fascinating insight into pre-Hispanic Mexico City (Tenochtitlán). Hire a private expert guide for a 2-hour curated tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Palacio Nacional to view Diego Rivera's monumental murals depicting the history of Mexico — a must-see masterpiece of Mexican art. Afterward, explore the charming neighborhood of Barrio Chino (Chinatown) and the historic market Mercado de San Juan, a gourmet market beloved by chefs, featuring premium cheeses, charcuterie, exotic fruits, and international delicacies.
day_by_day.evening: Evening visit to the iconic Torre Latinoamericana observation deck for panoramic city views at dusk, followed by a cocktail experience at Licorería Limantour (ranked among Latin America's best bars) in nearby Roma Norte, accessible by private car.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at El Cardenal — famous for their traditional Mexican breakfast including tamales, atole, and freshly baked pan dulce.
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at Mercado de San Juan — curate your own experience sampling premium oysters, Iberian ham, artisan cheeses, and Mexican craft beers or natural wines from the market's top vendors.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pujol — one of the world's top-ranked restaurants (reservations essential, book weeks ahead). Chef Enrique Olvera's tasting menu is a transformative celebration of Mexican culinary heritage and innovation.

day_by_day.notes: Book Pujol reservation well in advance — it is one of the most sought-after tables in Latin America. Private guide for Templo Mayor enhances the experience significantly. Comfortable walking shoes recommended for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Private chauffeur excursion to the Teotihuacán archaeological site (approximately 50km northeast, 1-hour drive). Arrive early to beat the crowds and climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon. A private archaeologist guide will bring the ancient Mesoamerican city to life with expert storytelling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and check out the upscale neighborhood of Polanco — Mexico City's answer to Paris's 16th arrondissement. Browse the high-end boutiques along Presidente Masaryk Avenue, visit the world-renowned Museo Soumaya (free entry) featuring an extraordinary collection of Rodin sculptures and European masters, and explore the adjacent Museo Jumex for cutting-edge contemporary art.
day_by_day.evening: Leisurely evening in Polanco with cocktails at the iconic Camino Real or a sophisticated mezcal tasting session at a curated mezcalería, experiencing artisanal mezcals from Oaxaca and beyond.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — request a packed premium breakfast or thermos of coffee for the road if departing before 7:30am.
meals.lunch: Lunch at La Gruta, a spectacular restaurant set inside a natural cave near Teotihuacán — a uniquely atmospheric dining experience with traditional Mexican cuisine.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Quintonil in Polanco — Chef Jorge Vallejo's acclaimed restaurant celebrates contemporary Mexican cuisine with an emphasis on native ingredients and vegetables. Consistently ranked among the world's 50 best restaurants.

day_by_day.notes: Depart for Teotihuacán no later than 8:00am to enjoy the site before peak heat and crowds. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water — the pyramids involve significant sun exposure. Quintonil reservation should be made in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the bohemian and culturally rich neighborhoods of Coyoacán and San Ángel via private car (30 minutes south of Centro). Begin at the iconic Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul) — the vibrant blue house where Frida Kahlo was born and lived. Book timed-entry tickets in advance. Stroll the charming cobblestone streets of Coyoacán's colonial center and visit the lively Mercado de Coyoacán for artisan crafts and snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to San Ángel to visit the Museo Casa Estudio Diego Rivera y Frida Kahlo — the modernist dual studios designed by architect Juan O'Gorman. Browse the prestigious Bazar del Sábado artisan market (if visiting on a Saturday) or explore the neighborhood's art galleries and boutiques. Return to Centro Histórico via private transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a live performance of the Ballet Folklórico de México at the magnificent Palacio de Bellas Artes — a world-class showcase of traditional Mexican regional dance and music in one of the most beautiful concert halls in the Americas. Book premium orchestra seats.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Café El Jarocho in Coyoacán — a legendary local institution serving some of the best café de olla (traditional spiced coffee) in Mexico City, beloved by locals for decades.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Los Danzantes in Coyoacán — an elegant restaurant and mezcal bar in a beautiful colonial courtyard, offering refined Oaxacan-inspired cuisine and an exceptional mezcal selection.
meals.dinner: Pre-show dinner at Restaurante del Centro Cultural de Bellas Artes or post-show late dinner at Nicos — a beloved Mexico City classic known for preserving traditional Mexican recipes passed down through generations, with an outstanding wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: Ballet Folklórico performances typically run on Wednesdays and Sundays — confirm schedule and book premium seats in advance at the Bellas Artes box office or official website. Frida Kahlo Museum requires advance timed-entry ticket purchase online.

day_by_day.morning: Start the final day with a private culinary experience — join a premium morning market tour and hands-on cooking class with a renowned local chef. Visit a traditional tianguis or Mercado de la Merced to source fresh chiles, herbs, and local produce, then return to a private kitchen to prepare classic Mexican dishes such as mole, tamales, or chiles en nogada.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Centro Histórico for last-minute exploration and souvenir shopping. Visit Casa de los Azulejos (House of Tiles) — a stunning 18th-century palace covered in Talavera tiles, now home to a Sanborns restaurant and cultural space. Browse the artisan shops along República de Uruguay Street for premium folk art, Talavera pottery, and silver jewelry. Visit the Palacio de Correos (Postal Palace) for its breathtaking iron-and-glass interior.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a top-tier restaurant celebrating the best of the trip. Enjoy a final mezcal or tequila toast reflecting on five extraordinary days in one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before the morning market tour.
meals.lunch: Enjoy the fruits of your culinary class as your midday meal — a deeply personal and memorable dining experience.
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Sud 777 or Rosetta — Chef Elena Reygadas's Rosetta in Roma Norte is a landmark of modern Mexican cuisine with Italian influences, set in a gorgeous early 20th-century mansion. An unforgettable final meal.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure logistics with hotel concierge — arrange private luxury transfer to airport based on flight time. Pack any artisan purchases carefully; Talavera ceramics and silver jewelry make exceptional premium souvenirs. Consider tipping your private guides and drivers generously — 15–20% is customary for premium service in Mexico City.
